subject.title: In-turn background work (Workflow / run_in_background / Workflow-backed skills) is SIGKILLed at the turn boundary under the claude-cli runtime

question: Should claude-cli support Workflow-backed background work with a durable host and completion route, or should OpenClaw explicitly refuse that background contract on claude-cli until such support exists?
rationale: The remaining work crosses claude-cli process lifetime, native-tool policy, task registry delivery, and channel/session routing, so automation cannot safely choose the public contract or compatibility posture.

options.title: Fail closed for now
options.body: Extend the current Bash/Monitor denial posture to any unsupported claude-cli background contract and surface a clear user-visible refusal until durable hosting exists.

options.title: Implement durable support
options.body: Build a persistent or detached claude-cli background host that snapshots origin session/channel/thread and persists completion before delivery.

options.title: Split the tracker
options.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella while delegating delivery ownership to #80450/#94153 and tracking claude-cli refusal/support in a narrower runtime issue.

recommendation.title: Fail closed for now
recommendation.body: Extend the current Bash/Monitor denial posture to any unsupported claude-cli background contract and surface a clear user-visible refusal until durable hosting exists.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus owns the clearest feature-history trail for claude-cli live-session process lifetime and also merged the native background-tool denial PR.
